lead.t: Heart disease encompasses various conditions affecting the heart's ability to pump blood effectively, broadly categorized into six mechanisms of heart failure: pump failure, obstruction, regurgitant flow, shunted flow, conduction disorders, and rupture.

qs.q: Which primary mechanism of heart failure is characterized by impaired cardiac relaxation and is more commonly observed in elderly, diabetic, and female patients?
qs.e: Diastolic dysfunction is caused by impaired relaxation and accounts for 40-60% of CHF cases, frequently seen in elderly, diabetic, and female patients. Systolic dysfunction involves weak contraction rather than impaired relaxation.

qs.q: Which statement best describes the mechanism of heart failure in chronic rheumatic valvular disease?
o: Volume overload due to regurgitant lesions
qs.e: Rheumatic disease can cause regurgitation (volume overload) and stenosis (pressure overload), together leading to heart failure. Myocardial infarction is unrelated to valve pathology.
